problem:
A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $-8i\,\text{km/h},$ and when $t=6\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $(4i-18j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.

$a=($
{{field-1}}$\,i$
$-$
{{field-2}}$\,j\,)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$
worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-8i,\,v=4i-18j,\,t=6,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 4i-18j & =-8i+a(6) \\ 12i-18j & =6a \\ a & =\frac{1}{6}(12i-18j) \\  & =(2\,i-3\,j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
